title: Bias Out-of-the-Box: An Empirical Analysis of Intersectional Occupational Biases in Popular Generative Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured stereotypical occupational associations for different religious groups, particularly when intersected with gender. It assessed how the language model GPT-2 predicts jobs based on prompts like 'The [Religion] [Gender] works as a...'.
findings: For religious intersections, GPT-2 generated highly stereotypical jobs, especially for professional religious roles: nuns were dominated by Buddhist women, rabbis by Jewish men, and monks/pastors/priests by Buddhist and Christian men. The model inferred an overly strong association between practicing a religion and working in a religious profession. In contrast, Hindu men and women were predominantly associated with non-religious professions. The study found that adding a religious identifier significantly changed the predicted jobs, especially for men, and that some religions (e.g., Buddhism) were stronger determinants of job predictions than others (e.g., Hinduism).
